metadata.topic: Thermal Physics — Energy Lost by Water and Specific Latent Heat of Fusion of Ice
metadata.note: Q3ci 3m: Q_water = mcΔT = 200×4.2×22 = 18480 J. Q3cii 3m: L = Q/m_ice = 18480/60 = 308 J/g = 308 J g⁻¹. Combined. Assume all heat lost by water = heat gained by ice.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q3c(i/ii) — Thermal Energy Lost by Water and Latent Heat of Fusion of Ice
question.text:
A thermometer is placed in a plastic cup containing 200 g of water at 22 °C. Small pieces of ice at 0 °C are added until the temperature of the mixture reaches 0 °C. The total mass of ice added was 60 g. The specific heat capacity of water is 4.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹.

(i) Calculate the thermal energy lost by the original volume of water. (3 marks)

(ii) Assume all the thermal energy lost by the water is transferred to the ice. Calculate the specific latent heat of fusion of ice. (3 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Q3c(i) — Energy lost by water:

Q = mcΔT = 200 g × 4.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹ × (22 − 0) °C = 200 × 4.2 × 22 = 18 480 J

Q3c(ii) — Specific latent heat of fusion:

Q = mL → L = Q/m = 18 480 / 60 = 308 J g⁻¹ = 308 000 J kg⁻¹

Context: The accepted value of L_f for ice is about 334 J g⁻¹ — the experiment gives 308 J g⁻¹, slightly low due to heat losses to the cup and surroundings.

steps.label:
Water: m = 200 g | c = 4.2 J/(g·°C) | Δθ = 22 − 0 = 22 °C
Ice: m_ice = 60 g
Formulas: Q = mcΔθ (sensible heat) | Q = mL (latent heat, no temperature change)
Calculate the thermal energy lost by the 200 g of water. (3 marks)
Calculate the specific latent heat of fusion of ice. (3 marks)
